subject: Request: temporary split-shift P1/P2 response window for overnight UTC coverage
messages:
From: Lydia Price <lydia@fintegro.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.k@fintegro.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Overnight SLA concern — P1 response gap and temporary ask

Hi Jonas / Ben,

Quick note from the Fintegro SRE team: over the last three weeks we've observed a spike in overnight P1 incidents (00:00–06:00 UTC) where our current on-call rotation at Redwood has a known handoff gap because the on-call engineer typically signs out at 23:00 UTC local. The result is our SREs waiting longer for a first response; three incidents crossed the 30-minute P1 window last month.

We understand Redwood's standard SLA and that staffing is managed globally, but given our production migration next week (2027-05-06) we need a short-term mitigation plan. Specifically, can Redwood provide a temporary P1 response exception that guarantees a first acknowledgement within 20 minutes for incidents from 00:00–06:00 UTC for the period 2027-05-03 to 2027-05-10?

If a time-boxed exception isn't possible, we would accept a proposed split-shift or staggered on-call where a second engineer covers 00:00–04:00 UTC. Also request a confirmed escalation path to a manager within 45 minutes if the issue is not being actively triaged.

We raised a HubSpot ticket earlier (HS-98764) and have a short runbook we'd share. I can hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Lydia Price
Director, Site Reliability — Fintegro
[Attachment: fintegro-prod-incidents-summary.csv (CSV)]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Price <lydia@fintegro.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Overnight SLA concern — P1 response gap and temporary ask

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear summary and the HS reference. We've pulled the incident logs on our side and see the same pattern during the UTC night window.

Short answer: we can propose a time-limited exception but need internal approval and a clear on-call plan. Proposed immediate options:
- Option A (preferred): Temporary split-shift for 2027-05-03 -> 2027-05-10 with two overlapping engineers (one covering 22:00–02:00 UTC, second covering 02:00–06:00 UTC). This reduces the single-engineer burnout and preserves 20-min P1 acknowledgement.
- Option B: Maintain current rota but escalate automatically to an on-call manager after 30 minutes with a guaranteed acknowledgement within 45 minutes.

I've attached a draft rota and a short change-control note for legal/compliance review. Can you confirm which option Fintegro prefers? If you want Option A, we'll need a quick sign-off on the proposed rota and a pull-through contact for escalation (name + mobile).

I'll loop in Marissa for SLA exception approval; Ben can help operationalize the rota. If you want a call, I'm available 30–60 minutes from now.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-shift-rota.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lydia Price <lydia@fintegro.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Overnight SLA concern — P1 response gap and temporary ask

Thanks everyone — I reviewed the incident pattern and Jonas's proposed options. From a support / SRE policy perspective, I'm willing to approve a time-limited exception to the standard P1 acknowledgement window under the following conditions:

1) Scope & duration: 2027-05-03 00:00 UTC through 2027-05-10 23:59 UTC.
2) Commitment: Redwood will ensure a first acknowledgement within 20 minutes for P1s during 00:00–06:00 UTC by implementing Option A (split-shift overlap).
3) Staffing: Ben will publish the on-call rota and confirm names and phone numbers by EOD 2027-05-01.
4) Escalation path: if a P1 is not actively triaged within 30 minutes, the on-call engineer escalates to Support Manager (Marissa Cole) and then to Head of Ops (Vivek Kulkarni) at 45 minutes. Contact numbers will be included in the rota.
4a) If issue impacts data privacy or sustained availability (>2 hours), we will trigger the executive notification chain immediately.
5) Compliance: Fintegro agrees to the attached change-control acknowledgement and will not expand the exception beyond the agreed dates without 48-hour prior notice.

Ben — please produce the final rota and a short onboarding note for Fintegro SREs. Lydia — if the dates or scope above look off, flag them now. Otherwise, we will proceed with Option A and treat this as a formal SLA exception with the stated guardrails.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Support — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: change-control.pdf (PDF)]
From: Lydia Price <lydia@fintegro.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Overnight SLA concern — P1 response gap and temporary ask

Marissa / Jonas / Ben — this is perfect, thanks. Fintegro accepts the temporary exception and the proposed dates. We'll sign the change-control acknowledgement and provide Rajesh (SRE lead) as the primary escalation contact: Rajesh Kumar +1 415-555-0198.

Next steps for us: we will upload the signed acknowledgement to HS-98764 and confirm any additional runbook notes by 2027-05-01 16:00 UTC. Please confirm once the rota is published.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Lydia
Director, Site Reliability — Fintegro
